title: Position-based rule matcher fallback only engages when query comparison yields >1 candidates
answers: Why doesn't the rule matcher fall back to position when the query hash matches nothing?
Rule matcher has no fallback for zero query matches
getMatchingRulerRule gives no match even though the rule exists
body:
Invariant (currently a known gap, not yet fixed): the ruler-to-Prometheus rule matcher only consults the rule's position-in-group as a tiebreaker when the query-based comparison returns more than one candidate; when it returns zero candidates (e.g. because hashQuery fingerprints diverged) there is no fallback and the rule is reported unmatched on both sides.
Where enforced: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/ruleMatching.ts matching logic used by getMatchingRulerRule / matchRulesGroup.
If you fix a new hashQuery normalization gap, this zero-candidate case is still a silent failure mode worth checking against - the PR author explicitly flagged extending the position fallback to zero candidates as unfinished follow-up work.

search: The ruler-to-Prometheus rule matcher uses rule position-in-group as a tiebreaker only when query-based comparison returns more than one candidate, not when it returns zero. This means if hashQuery fingerprints diverge and no query-match is found, the rule is silently reported unmatched on both sides without consulting the position fallback. The logic is located in ruleMatching.ts (getMatchingRulerRule, matchRulesGroup) and represents a known gap where extending the position fallback to zero-candidate cases is flagged as unfinished follow-up work. When fixing hashQuery normalization gaps, explicitly test the zero-candidate case to detect this failure mode.
